clue.text: Punk has to ward off evil

blocks.note: first meaning: rotten wood used as tinder
second meaning: the phrase people say, tapping timber, to avert bad luck

explanation.surface: A punk rocker sets out to keep evil at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Punk is an old word for decayed wood that smoulders, used for lighting fires; it has nothing to do with the music here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rotten timber used as kindling is called punk, and saying the superstitious phrase while knocking on timber is meant to avert bad luck.

clue.text: Oddly, took views that were slithy

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for the creatures Lewis Carroll called slithy

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep only the characters in the first, third, fifth positions and so on

blocks.note: first and third letters
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Someone oddly took a view of things that were slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: The line "'Twas brillig, and the slithy toves" opens Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem Jabberwocky.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's Jabberwocky the nonsense creatures described with the invented adjective slithy are toves, so the clause identifies them.

clue.text: Discourage private, removing his leader before Continental victory

indicators.note: taking away the leader means dropping the opening letter of the soldier's title

blocks.note: a gunner is a private soldier in the artillery
VE is Victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: A soldier, with his commander gone, is dispirited ahead of victory in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Private suggests secret, but it is a rank: an artillery private is a gunner. Continental here means on the European mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to sap their nerve and confidence, which is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Man approaching battlefield to give command that's tricky

blocks.note: a man is referred to as he
the Belgian town fought over in the First World War
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier nearing the front line issues an awkward order.
explanation.walkthrough: Ypres in Flanders was the scene of several great battles of 1914-18.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror calls out this exclamation at the moment a trick is completed, so it is the command of a magic act.

clue.text: Delighted cow went here

definitions.note: a place phrase, standing for where the nursery-rhyme cow jumped

blocks.note: first meaning: extremely happy
second meaning: where the cow jumped in Hey Diddle Diddle

explanation.surface: A cow is thrilled about where it went.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme Hey Diddle Diddle the cow jumped over the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being thrilled is the same phrase that, taken literally, places the leaping cow of the nursery rhyme above the lunar body.

clue.text: Duck can be found in duck-pond, I presume

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: the end of pond, the word I and the start of presume

explanation.surface: A duck is likely to be found on the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck someone or something is to plunge it briefly under water, a quick immersion or dunking.

clue.text: Brooke's said to be a poet

indicators.note: said means we take the surname as it sounds when spoken, not as written

blocks.note: the poet's name spoken sounds like brooks, small streams

explanation.surface: Rupert Brooke's reputation is that of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooke looks like the poet of the definition, but he only supplies a sound: streams. Burn is the Scots word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns, the national poet of Scotland, wrote Auld Lang Syne and many other verses in Scots.

clue.text: Is extravagant with music

blocks.note: first meaning: squanders money, as in blueing one's savings
second meaning: the melancholy genre born in the American South

explanation.surface: Someone splashes out on music.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue money is an old British way of saying to spend it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb blue means to squander cash, and the noun names the African-American musical genre of sorrowful songs.

clue.text: Jehu showed the way to be greedy

blocks.note: a road is a way
to hog is to take more than one's share

explanation.surface: A biblical king led people to be grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: Jehu in the Bible 'driveth furiously', so a jehu came to mean a reckless driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, inconsiderate motorist who takes up the whole carriageway is a modern equivalent of the furious biblical charioteer.

clue.text: A risky business, to turn up without final witness

indicators.note: without its final means the closing character is dropped
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: short for speculation, a gamble
to rotate is to turn

explanation.surface: A gamble that fails to turn up for its finale.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTATE loses its E and is then read upwards as TATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker or eyewitness watches events happen, so a person in the crowd is a synonym.

clue.text: Artist shows military leaders what a trench looks like

blocks.note: the van, or vanguard, leads an army
a dyke can be a ditch

explanation.surface: A painter depicts generals and their trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony van Dyck, the Flemish painter at the court of Charles I, is often anglicised in this spelling.

clue.text: Outer covering of fruit — date

blocks.note: a plum is a fruit
a date can be a period or age

explanation.surface: The skin of a fruit called a date.
explanation.walkthrough: Date looks like the fruit, but it is the time sense: an era.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers form its external coat, the layer that covers and protects its body.

clue.text: Still more aggrieved when love is rejected by king

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the god's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: Eros is the god of love
R for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A spurned lover is even more upset after a king turns them down.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is usually O in crosswords; here it is the Greek god, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: more hurt or resentful, more painful, still angrier than before.

clue.text: A truism, there's no more to be said

definitions.text: there's no more to be said

blocks.note: first meaning: a statement true by its very form, saying a thing is itself

blocks.clueFragment: there's no more to be said
blocks.note: second meaning: the phrase that closes a discussion

explanation.surface: Someone states the obvious and ends the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a tautology, plainly true of anything, and it is also the idiom used to declare a matter settled.

clue.text: Not believing that Alice is artificial

indicators.note: artificial means made up, so the letters are put together in a new way

blocks.note: eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that Alice is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective describes someone who denies the existence of any god, hence lacking religious faith.

clue.text: Read out letter's last words dramatically

indicators.note: reading out loud means we use the spoken sound of the letter's name

blocks.note: the seventeenth letter of the alphabet, spoken

explanation.surface: Someone reads aloud the final lines of a letter with theatrical flair.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter looks like a piece of correspondence; it is an alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre, the closing words of one actor's speech signal the next performer to speak or enter.

clue.text: President gives one up daily

indicators.note: to give something up is to surrender it, so a letter leaves the title
completes the phrase give up, meaning to relinquish part of the word

blocks.note: a woman who presides over a meeting
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A president quits a post every day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily, in British usage, is a domestic cleaner employed by the day, the same job as this older word.

clue.text: Appear to undergo conversion

blocks.note: first meaning: be born or come into public view
second meaning: suddenly understand or accept a faith

explanation.surface: Someone seems to be changing their beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means coming into existence or public notice, and also a sudden realisation or religious awakening.

clue.text: After having a friend on the side

blocks.note: later means after
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone, later on, takes a lover on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideways or towards the flank, this adverb describes movement or position at the side.

clue.text: Palgrave, for instance, has left 18 in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means thrown into disorder, so the letters get muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
L for left
the answer to 18 down

explanation.surface: Francis Palgrave has abandoned a London district in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Palgrave compiled The Golden Treasury, the Victorian collection of English lyric poems. Tooting is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Palgrave is an example of someone who compiles collections of poems, so he exemplifies the compiler the answer names.

clue.text: Attracting attention in London

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a place in the capital

blocks.note: first meaning: sounding a horn to be noticed
second meaning: a district of south London

explanation.surface: Someone is drawing notice in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooting is a residential district in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooting a car horn draws notice, and the same word names an area of south-west London.

clue.text: Dry atmosphere

blocks.note: first meaning: hang laundry out to ... it
second meaning: the gases around us

explanation.surface: The climate is arid.
explanation.definitionFit: To air clothes is to dry them out, and the gaseous mixture we breathe is the atmosphere.

clue.text: All right — I'll admit it quickly

indicators.note: will admit means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the ego is the self, I
R for right

explanation.surface: Someone confesses hastily that it is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The it of the clue points back to right, which goes inside EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical scores this Italian tempo marking tells players to perform briskly, at a lively pace.

clue.text: In which I hunt down crooks

definitions.text: In which I hunt down crooks

indicators.note: crooks read as a verb means bends, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A detective narrator describes the story in which they track down criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the detective story is where the sleuth hunts criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective novel is a book where an investigator, often telling the tale, tracks down the guilty party.

clue.text: Ship about to be wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A vessel is about to run aground.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the World Wars is a type of naval vessel, so it is an instance of a ship.

clue.text: Foreign football regulations

blocks.note: first meaning: Australian ..., the code played Down Under
second meaning: laws governing conduct

explanation.surface: The laws of football as played abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Australian rules football, often just called Aussie Rules, is a distinct code played mainly in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians call their own football code by this short name, and the plain word also means laws or regulations.

clue.text: Mark's second kiss

blocks.note: S for second
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A man called Mark gives a second kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name, but it is the definition: a small spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spot or blemish on a surface is a small mark, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: I do more to make money

indicators.note: to make something is to fashion it, so the letters are built into a new shape

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A worker promises to put in extra effort to earn cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old Portuguese gold coin once common in Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This Portuguese gold coin circulated widely in eighteenth-century England, so it is an example of currency.

clue.text: Decline to live up to a brilliant start

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from the bottom
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone fails to match a promising early career.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding of the tide gives the verb for falling away or waning, so to diminish or decline.

clue.text: Move around in Lancashire town or city

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the short verb is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Colne is a mill town in Lancashire
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Someone moves about a northern English town or city.
explanation.walkthrough: Colne is a small town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The German metropolis on the Rhine, famed for its cathedral and its scented water, is a city.

clue.text: Black or possibly white piece, we hear

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun; night is black

indicators.note: we hear means the chess word is used for its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a chess piece that may be white, said aloud

explanation.surface: A chess piece that might be black or white.
explanation.walkthrough: Black or white suggests both are chess colours; Black is the definition and only white belongs to the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are black, so the noun for the dark period is clued by the colour.

clue.text: By dressing, I'll turn up in a hat

indicators.note: dressing means clothing something, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe
to cock a brim is to turn it up

explanation.surface: Someone getting dressed says they will show up wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A billycock is a bowler-type hat with a round crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-crowned felt hat, much like a bowler, worn by Victorian working men, is a kind of hat.
